sources.excerpt: GOLDEN PLEXI- Plexi Style Distortion-TONE CITY ▏Analog Pedals & Power supplies PRODUCTS MINI Overdrive Nashiville Sweet Cream Bad Horse Mandragora Blues Man Noble Man Dry Martini Kaffir Lime Distortion/Fuzz London Bender Golden Plexi Wild Fire Matcha Cream Fuxx Fuzz Black Tea Mickey Delay/Reverb/Chorus Tape Machine Angel Wing Tiny Spring Phaser/Tremelo Summer orange Tremble Compressor/Boost Buzz Bee Comp Engine All Spark DELUXE Heavenly Lake-Reverb&Delay King of Blues-Overdrive Model M-Distortion Holy Aura-Distortion Big Rumble-Overdrive CUSTOM Durple - Overdrive Wildfro-Distortion Lilheat-Overdrive Double Durple-OD&Boost TPS TPS-5 TPS-6 TPS-8 TPS-10 TPS-12 POWER STICK LEGEND Green Tube Blue Crystal Golden Face ULTIMATE 龍 LOONG ARTISTS COMMUNITY YouTube Instagram Facebook SUPPORT Certification TEST & REPORT E-CATALOGUE E-MANUAL DISTRIBUTOR ABOUT US CONTACT CN EN HOME - PRODUCTS - MINI GOLDEN PLEXI- Plexi Style Distortion Input Impendence: 500K Output Impendence:10K Current Draw: 15 mA Power Supply: DC 9V adapter DM.: 9.4(L)*4.5(W)*4.8(H) (cm) N.W.: 0.27kg True Bypass Product Description Gear Demos Related Gear Manual & Report Where to buy Golden Plexi is a classic rock amp sound with a timeless plexi-style tone lifted from the very best legendary black and gold amplifiers. In 2022, we refined the gain structure of the Golden Plexi to provide a more focused and consistent high-gain dynamic response, renaming it the Golden Plexi2. While this version received excellent feedback, we also heard many requests for the return of the original Golden Plexi—with its wider adjustable high-gain range.Realizing that we should not let people miss out on this amazing"mini-pedal miracle," the original version Golden Plexi is back for the 2025 version, and it renamed as name: Golden Plexi. An added toggle switch allows users to switch the tone from a right side tightened gain ( Golden Plexi 2) to left side more high gain and bass (low gain). This version also optimizes the high frequencies in TONE. It's actually very quiet. While there are only four controls on this mini pedal, we has incorporated the essentials. The volume control acts as you would normally expect, with the tone and gain control shaving a wider range than you would expect. Delivering everything from a sweet crunch to crushing high-gain, this versatile pedal lets you attain fantastic tones suitable for blues, rock and metal. The sensitivity of the tone control means that you can run this pedal into the clean channel of nearly any amplifier and get the classic plexi sound you are craving. Keep the control low for a smooth lead tone, or crank it higher for a more cutting sound that'll pierce through nicely in a mix. This is an mini wonders that worth your trying. sources.excerpt: Golden Plexi V3 by Tone City | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE Tone City Golden Plexi V3 LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS DISTORTION Description The Golden Plexi is a classic rock amp sound cranked up to eleven, with a timeless Plexi-style tone inspired by the very best legendary black-and-gold amps. In 2022, we created an updated version of the Golden Plexi with a tighter and improved gain structure, offering a more focused sound with enhanced dynamics. We called it the Golden Plexi 2, and it has been very popular since its launch. The 2025 version features an added toggle switch that allows users to switch between the classic Golden Plexi tone and the Golden Plexi 2 tone. This version also optimizes the high frequencies in the tone for a low signal -to-noise ratio. The volume control works as you would expect, and the tone and gain controls have a wider range than usual. Delivering everything from sweet crunch to crushing high gain, this versatile pedal lets you achieve fantastic tones suitable for blues, rock, and metal. Thanks to the sensitivity of the tone control, you can use this pedal with the clean channel of almost any amplifier to achieve the classic Plexi sound. Keep the controls low for a smooth lead tone or turn them up for a more cutting sound that will stand out in a mix. Tone City Tone City Mini series browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal browse by enclosure mini pedal Tone City TC-T7 Golden Plexi v2 - British Distortion Published on September 2, 2025 Tone City Mini series distortion mini pedal pedal Information The Tone City Golden Plexi 2 is a compact distortion pedal designed to emulate the iconic tone of vintage British rock amplifiers. Inspired by the legendary "plexi" sound, this updated version offers a refined gain structure that delivers improved focus and dynamic response, making it suitable for everything from smooth blues to aggressive rock and metal. Featuring a straightforward three-knob layout, the Golden Plexi 2 provides intuitive control over volume, tone, and gain. The gain range spans from mild crunch to high-gain distortion, while the highly sensitive tone knob allows precise sculpting of high frequencies. Whether running into a clean amp or part of a larger effects chain, the Golden Plexi 2 delivers the classic amp-in-a-box experience in a pedalboard-friendly format. Built using analog circuitry and housed in a durable mini enclosure, the pedal operates via 9V DC power and features true bypass switching for transparent signal integrity. Show original Tone City Golden Plexi Review 3 かける 2026年1月8日 23:14 Introduction I have reviewed this in other articles as well, but I have grown to like it so much that I have no intention of letting it go as my main distortion pedal. I wanted this review to reach people who are looking for this type of distortion ( Marshall JCM800 / 1959 style), so I decided to write a standalone review. I have also posted a similar review on a certain music store site. Main Subject I originally liked the BOSS GT-1 built-in Marshall 1959 preamp, and based on my musical tastes (garage, punk, alternative), I vaguely thought, "I want a crunchy to overdrive level of gain with this kind of jagged sound." After doing some research, I learned that the 1959 is called a Plexi-style amp, so I started searching exclusively for pedals like that. However, for some reason, there are hardly any demo videos of effects pedals out there that feature someone strumming chords. Most are just single-note playing. Why? I think there is a demand for chord sounds, too. That's when I found this video. They were demoing it with the vibe of music I like, which was very helpful. I thought, "This is the sound I've been looking for!" and since it was inexpensive, I decided to buy it. I bought it at Sound House. It was 7,480 yen brand new. The GAIN knob lights up in blue. When I bought it, the photo was of the Ver.2, but what arrived was the Ver.3. It allowed switching between Ver.1 and Ver.2 specifications using a MOD switch. Carl Martin PlexiTone clone, it seems. I prefer this design. It also seems to have its own uniqueness due to the MOD switch. Depending on the environment, with a single-coil pickup, the GAIN goes from a low-gain crunch at minimum to 7:30, overdrive from 7:30 to just before 9:00, and distortion-level gain beyond that. It produces a shimmering distortion with edge in both the lows and highs. The strong crunch sound, in particular, has a glassy and metallic resonance; if you set the GAIN to around 7:30 and play chords with the neck single-coil pickup, you can get a sound like the backing track in the intro of " Stairway Generation / Base Ball Bear ". It also suits bridge single-coil pickups and humbucker pickups. If you turn up the GAIN, it combines with the thick sound of a humbucker for a very aggressive tone. I got the impression that it could handle hard rock and the like. The crunchiness was very good. In my environment, the TONE knob feels like the highs are too harsh at 12 o'clock. I keep mine at 9 o'clock. The mids are a bit thin, so if you are playing a solo, you might want to connect a booster that pushes the mids. The MOD switch seems to set it to Ver.1 specs when moved to the left, and Ver.2 specs when moved to the right. The former felt like it had slightly longer sustain and thicker lows compared to the latter, but the difference isn't big enough to notice immediately upon hearing it. I basically use Ver.2, and use the Ver.1 setting when I want a thicker sound than usual. I tested it with tube amps ( Peavey 6505+ ) and transistor amps (Marshall MG100HDFX , JC120 , Pathfinder10 ), and I think it is usable with both. (The large amps are the ones in the university club room.) I have only ever played tube Marshall types on amp simulators, but it feels less like the Marshall 1959 that the Plexi style is derived from, and more like a version of it that makes it easier to increase the gain and use. It feels close to a Marshall JCM800 , but I felt the sound was slightly different. If you want an edgy Marshall -style distortion, I definitely feel this is the one. Postscript There are many inexpensive options for effects pedals these days.
